$comment: Machine-readable record of how Reykjavík's citizen-report form behaves. This file is the source of truth: scripts/send-report.mjs, the Worker adapter and .github/workflows/contract.yml all read it, and the markdown under docs/research/ is generated from it where it repeats these values. Every claim carries how and when it was established, because none of it is documented by the city and all of it can change without notice. Re-verify with: node scripts/send-report.mjs --category ruslafotur --probe, which .github/workflows/contract.yml also runs daily
source: black-box probing of the live site; no city documentation exists

submit.notes: No cookie, CSRF token, captcha or Origin check. The ?cat= step is presentational and 308-redirects here.
submit.method_of_verification: curl with an empty payload returned 400 with the validator's own envelope

successResponse.confirmationEmail: from no-reply@reykjavik.is, repeats the number in Icelandic, English and Polish
successResponse.howEstablished: accidentally, by report 110474 — see docs/incidents/2026-08-21-filed-a-real-report.md. Never establish anything this way again.

addressSearch.notes: Staðfangaskrá passed through. We read the registry directly instead — see decisions/0004.

addressInfo.notes: Under /abendingar/, not /location/ beside its sibling. Both params required. Returns an empty array, not an error, for an address the register does not hold.

files.maxCountClientNotes: measured 2026-08-29 by handing the picker six files over CDP: five reached the submitted field, the counter read 5/5, and the sixth was dropped with NO error text anywhere on the page. So it is a real cap and a silent one — somebody who selects six photographs is told about five. It is the CLIENT's cap: the submitted input carries no limit of its own and the server's file count is still unknown.
files.acceptLivesOnThePicker: the accept list is an attribute of the hidden picker input (opacity 0, the one the dropzone clicks), NOT of the input named `files` that goes on the wire — that one has no accept attribute at all. So the MIME allowlist is a browser-side courtesy and a direct POST is not held to it, which is consistent with the city validating only `description`. Measured 2026-08-29.
files.noUploadOnSelect: choosing a file sends nothing. Measured 2026-08-29 with every non-GET failed at the browser and watched: attaching six photographs produced zero blocked requests, so the bytes travel only with the submit.
files.notes: HEIC is absent from the list and it is what an iPhone shoots by default, so the iOS capture path has to transcode before it can send; measured 2026-08-22 on an iPhone 13 original, transcoding grew the file rather than shrank it

email.clientValidation: none. Measured 2026-08-29 from the DOM: the field is type="text" (not type="email"), with no `required` and no `pattern`. Nothing in the browser checks it, so a typo is accepted silently and the confirmation simply never arrives — which is why our own rule is in the app (#163, decision 0015).
email.notes: the only way the reporter hears anything back. The form asks for it under "Viltu fylgjast með ábendingunni þinni?" and offers no other channel: there is no phone field anywhere on the form, so an address is the whole of what the city can answer to. Confirmed from the rendered form on 2026-08-29 as well as from the element list.
email.ourRule: required by us — see validation.onlyDescriptionIsEnforced. A report with no address reaches the queue and its reporter is never told anything by the city; report 110474 got a reply, and a request number, only because a human had typed one in (docs/incidents/2026-08-21-filed-a-real-report.md). Enforced in the apps, not yet in the relay (#163).

confirmationEmail.how: received, and kept as a file, for the project's one deliberate real submission (decision 0006, reference 110759). The 2026-08-21 accidental report 110474 produced an identical message, so both samples are held and the format is stable across nine days.
confirmationEmail.subject: Takk fyrir að senda ábendinguna <category display name> til Reykjavíkurborgar.
confirmationEmail.echoesCategoryDisplayName: the subject and all three bodies name the CATEGORY the report was filed under, in the city's own display form — so the confirmation is the one place a reporter could notice a category chosen wrongly.
confirmationEmail.statedServiceTarget: answer the report, or forward it to the right specialist, within the next working day. A second email is promised when an answer exists.
confirmationEmail.timing: stamped 01:18:02Z, which is 1.9 s BEFORE the relay finished reading the city's 200 at 01:18:03.881Z. So the mail is queued while the submission is still being processed rather than after it is answered — OR the two clocks differ, which a Date header with second granularity cannot rule out. A draft of this line read the pair as 'sent as the form answers, not later', which is a causal claim the timestamps do not support in that direction; what they do support is that the confirmation is not sent later.
confirmationEmail.notes: this is the direct proof of what fields.email.notes previously argued from one accidental report. The address is the whole of the channel back, and it works.

onlyDescriptionIsEnforced.evidence: an empty POST returns {"error":"Missing required fields","inputErrors":{"description":[…]}} and names nothing else
onlyDescriptionIsEnforced.consequence: the city would accept a report with no coordinate; our relay must reject one
onlyDescriptionIsEnforced.notTested: whether a description-only report actually succeeds — a request that passes validation files a real report

unknownSlugReturns400NotFound404.evidence: a nonsense slug returns 400 with an empty body; an English slug on the Icelandic path returns 400 with a page titled 'Síða fannst ekki (404)'; an empty slug returns 405
unknownSlugReturns400NotFound404.consequence: status alone cannot distinguish a typo'd category from a missing description; the discriminator is 'Missing required fields' plus the category hidden field being re-rendered

theSubmitButtonIsNeverDisabled.evidence: measured 2026-08-29 from the DOM, with every non-GET failed at the browser: on an EMPTY form the Senda ábendingu button reports disabled=false, and with description and email filled while lat and lng are still empty strings it reports disabled=false and aria-disabled=null, on a form that is not noValidate. The description textarea is not marked required either.
theSubmitButtonIsNeverDisabled.corrects: docs/research/payload-map.md said lat and lng 'appear to be enforced in the browser only, by the map picker refusing to submit without a marker'. The picker does not refuse via the button, so whatever that sentence described is not the disabled state.
theSubmitButtonIsNeverDisabled.notTested: whether an onSubmit handler would refuse the send anyway — establishing that means pressing the button, which is decision 0006. So this narrows where the guard is NOT; it does not prove there is none.
theSubmitButtonIsNeverDisabled.consequence: nothing observable in the browser stops a report with no coordinate, and the server does not either. Our relay is the only thing that does.

noAddressFieldInPayload.evidence: the form's element list carries no address input; the search only moves the map marker, and moving the marker clears the search field
noAddressFieldInPayload.consequence: a thing with no address, which is the case this project exists for, is ordinary usage

map.$comment: A panning limit for the widget, not a jurisdiction check. Read from BrowserMap-*.js, whose filename hash changes on every deploy.

categoryNotes.taxonomyIsFlat: no category hands off to another system; only two carry an informational panel
categoryNotes.nodeIdGapsMeaning: six siblings were created with these and are no longer published; the list is editorial and can grow back
categoryNotes.localeChangesWhatTheCityReceives: the English form at /en/suggestion/send-suggestion/{enSlug} submits category 'Waste bins' and summary 'Suggestion -> Waste bins'. Always post the Icelandic form; the people triaging these read Icelandic.

registry.$comment: The city's address endpoints are Staðfangaskrá unchanged — Laugavegur 1 matched the HMS export to the last decimal, and the city's district '0000' is the registry's SVFNR column. We read the registry ourselves via iceaddr-ts.
registry.client: iceaddr-ts on npm (MIT, https://github.com/gudrodur/iceaddr-ts), zero-dependency and edge-native. Depend on the published package, never on a local checkout.
registry.twoCountsAreNotAConflict: The two differ by 778 because they measure different things. Postcodes do not follow municipal boundaries: Reykjavikurborg includes Kjalarnes, which carries its own postcode. Use the SVFNR count when the question is jurisdiction and the postcode count when the question is what ships on the phone. The SVFNR breakdown per municipality is in docs/research/payload-map.md and has not been re-derived since it was first measured.
registry.jurisdictionRule: reverse-look the coordinate to its nearest address and read SVFNR; anything but 0000 is not Reykjavík's to fix

unknown: maximum upload SIZE — the client sets no maxSize, so the limit is the server's and finding it means uploading until something breaks. The file COUNT is no longer wholly unknown: the client caps at five (fields.files.maxCountClient, measured 2026-08-29), though the server's own limit is still untested

for scale rather than as an answer: real captures measured 2026-08-22 were 1.1 MB from a Galaxy A71 and 2.66 MB from a Galaxy S23 Ultra, so three photos from a recent phone approach 8 MB and the unknown limit is not academic

an iPhone 13 original measured 2026-08-22 was 4.14 MB as HEIC, 4.78 MB transcoded to JPEG at quality 90 and 3.30 MB at quality 80, so two iPhone photos at a faithful quality already pass 8 MB and the transcode setting decides whether a report fits

backend.$comment: Read passively from the confirmation email's headers. No probing.
backend.system: Drupal, behind the React Router front end
backend.evidence: X-Mailer: Drupal; the category picker carries Drupal node ids; data-drupal-link-system-path appears in the page HTML
backend.legacyHost: abendingar.reykjavik.is 301s to reykjavik.is/abendingar and answers with X-Powered-By: PHP/7.3.33 and PleskLin

measurement.$comment: The follow-through half of the project. The city publishes no report volume and no response times.
measurement.referenceNumberIsACounter: each number a real user's report comes back with is a free sample of the city's total volume; two samples spaced in time give the rate

reportVolume.method: the two reference numbers this project has legitimately caused, differenced over the time between them — exactly the free sample referenceNumberIsACounter describes.

samples.note: the accidental real report (docs/incidents/2026-08-21-filed-a-real-report.md), withdrawn the same evening

reportVolume.confidence: two points, so this is a rate and not a trend: it cannot see weekday/weekend shape, seasonality, or a burst. Both samples also sit at the same clock position by accident (20:18 and 01:18), which nothing about them makes meaningful.
reportVolume.assumption: that the number is a single global sequence, incremented once per report, with no gaps and no other consumer. Two samples cannot distinguish that from a counter shared with another system, and there is no way to check without more numbers — which we cannot generate, because generating one means filing a real report.
